exposure: maternal serum creatinine (m-sCr) concentrations before delivery
ratio of placental weight to birth weight (PW/BW ratio)
outcome: neonatal serum creatinine (n-sCr) concentrations within 24 h of birth
cohort: The study included 278 preterm neonates treated at the University of the Ryukyus Hospital between March 2012 and October 2022, excluding those with underlying diseases or conditions affecting hemodynamics.
finding: A regression equation was derived (n-sCr = 0.092 + 0.970 x m-sCr) showing maternal serum creatinine to be the most potent influencer of neonatal serum creatinine within 24 hours of birth, with the placental weight to birth weight ratio influencing the difference between neonatal and maternal serum creatinine.
cross-section timing: Neonatal serum creatinine measured within 24 hours of birth; maternal serum creatinine measured before delivery.
